McLaren.summary: McLaren’s front suspension has been tweaked to smooth out airflow, giving the car a more stable feel into the bends, while the front‑corner geometry has also been refined for sharper turn‑in. At the back, the rear corner setup has been altered to improve mechanical grip, helping the car stay planted under heavy braking. Together, these changes should translate into quicker cornering and more consistent tyre performance, key factors for a strong showing this weekend.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has reshaped the underside of the car – the floor fences now have a different tilt, the central “boat” section is wider and the front edge of the floor is shorter and angled more sharply, while the diffuser at the rear has been re‑profiled. All of these tweaks help smooth the airflow under the car, generating extra down‑force without adding drag, so the team can corner harder and defend better on the high‑speed sections of this weekend’s circuit. In short, the new floor work should give Ferrari a noticeable grip boost where it counts most.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull’s new floor edge adds a small vent just ahead of the rear tyre, smoothing airflow under the car and boosting down‑force where it counts most. The tweak should give the RB better grip out of the high‑speed corners, helping them defend positions and attack harder on this weekend’s circuit. In short, a cleaner‑running floor means more cornering speed and a stronger chance to stay ahead of the competition.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has added bigger openings to the front brake ducts and a larger exit on the rear‑engine cover to boost cooling on this circuit. The extra airflow helps keep the brakes and power unit at optimal temperatures, which should translate into more consistent grip and stronger performance throughout the weekend.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: The new front‑wing flap shape smooths the air hitting the car, giving it better grip into the corners. At the back, the team has swapped to a rear‑wing profile that reduces drag on the straights, boosting top‑speed. Together, these tweaks should help Racing Bulls hit the apex faster and fight for higher positions on this weekend’s circuit.

Sauber / Audi.summary: Sauber‑Audi has reshaped the middle part of the floor and the edges around the diffuser, giving the car a cleaner, more powerful “under‑body” that sticks to the track better. They’ve also fitted an all‑new rear wing, which should smooth out the car’s balance and give extra bite in the corners. Together these tweaks should boost grip and stability, helping the team extract more speed and confidence out of this weekend’s layout.
